result.summary: This PR replaces the LogWarning and LogError log levels with a single LogAlert level, keeping the old macros as deprecated aliases to avoid churn. It updates logging.cpp, util/log.h, developer-notes.md, tests, and mechanically renames LogWarning/LogError calls to LogAlert in node/blockstorage.cpp via a scripted-diff. The author explicitly marks it draft pending #34038 because warning/error levels are currently exposed to users via -loglevel.
result.problem: Node operators and developers currently have two log severity levels (warning, error) whose only practical difference is whether the node is shutting down, which the author argues is redundant and can be seen by whether the node stopped. Distinguishing them adds a decision node authors of log calls must make with little payoff.

open_concerns: ryanofsky's Concept -0: prefers keeping warning/error as separate (and conditional) levels and adding a distinct 'critical' level instead of unifying into 'alert'; this alternative design was not implemented.
The PR is explicitly gated on the outcome of #34038, which concerns how -loglevel exposes these levels to users.

result.card: This PR merges the LogWarning and LogError log levels into a single LogAlert level in the logging framework (src/util/log.h, src/logging.cpp), keeping the old macros as deprecated aliases, and mechanically renames call sites in node/blockstorage.cpp via a scripted-diff. The problem is a minor operator-facing redundancy: two severity levels whose only real distinction is whether the node subsequently shuts down. The author explicitly marked it draft pending #34038, which concerns how log levels are exposed via -loglevel, and has been silent for 196 days with the branch needing a rebase. The single reviewer, ryanofsky, gave a code-review ACK but stated 'Concept -0', preferring a different design that keeps warning/error separate and adds a new 'critical' level, a preference the author has not addressed. The PR also conflicts with several other open logging PRs, suggesting the logging area is in flux and this specific approach may not be the one that lands.
